content.content:
1	# Investigation notes: issue #230, web control surface on the remote port
2	
3	Read: CLAUDE.md, docs/lessons.md (generic architecture lessons, nothing remote-specific), docs/remote-client.md §4.1-4.4, §5, §9, the "Remote client" status section of docs/design.md (from line 3107), and the code named below. All line numbers are in this worktree.
4	
5	## On-disk record and rehydration (before the pane)
6	
7	Nothing new has to be persisted for the page itself.
8	- `identity.json` (server id, name, self-signed cert, SPKI hash, listen {lan, port}) and `devices.json` (`PairedDevice` in `src/ports/remote.rs:96`: id, name, scope, `token_sha256`, created, last_seen) already hold everything. A browser is one more `PairedDevice`; the host stores only the token's SHA-256 (`remote::token_sha256`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:345`).
9	- Rehydration of a paired browser = the token the browser keeps, looked up by hash on each request (`authenticate`, `src/app.rs:3127`, via `core.device_by_token`, `src/core/remote.rs:145`). Revocation removes the record, so the next request is 401 `unauthorized` "the token is not known; pair again" (`src/app.rs:3145`). The page can map that 401 to "revoked". The spec says revoke also closes the device's WebSocket.
10	- The browser-side record is new and lives on the device, not the host: wherever the token lives (an HttpOnly cookie, or storage), plus the pinned `server_id`/`spki_sha256` the page last saw, to say "identity changed, pair again". That is the only new state. If a cookie carries the token, the host needs no new field. If `Set-Cookie` attributes (Max-Age) matter, that is a host choice, not a record.
11	- Key rotation already deletes every device record (§5), so a browser's cookie or token goes stale in a way indistinguishable from revoke unless `/info` is compared: `/info` is the only unauthenticated place that can say the key changed.
12	- No `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump is implied unless `PairedDevice` gains a field (e.g. a `kind` or user agent string). The name from the user agent can go in the existing `name`.
13	- The pairing window is `never saved` state (`src/core/remote.rs` `pairing_at`, `pairing`), so a page opened with an expired code simply gets `pairing_closed` 403 from `/pair`.
14	
15	## Code the issue touches
16	
17	- `src/adapters/remote.rs`
18	  - `read_request` 444-516: parses request line, headers (lowercased), `authorization: Bearer` into `bearer`, upgrade key, query. It does not keep `cookie`, `user-agent`, `origin`, `host` or `sec-websocket-protocol` headers: `RemoteRequest` (360-372) has no field for them. Cookie/subprotocol auth and a user-agent device name each need a new field there. Header block is capped by `MAX_HEAD`.
19	  - `respond` 530-553: always `Content-Type: application/json`, no other headers, `Connection: keep-alive`, a fixed status reason table (no 302/304/etc.). Static files need a content type, CSP, `Cache-Control`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, and `Set-Cookie` on the pair reply, so this takes more than a body argument. `respond_upgrade` 519 has no subprotocol echo (needed if `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` is used; a browser closes the socket if the server does not echo one offered protocol).
20	  - `connection` 770-875: the rate check `Limits::limited` (633-640) keys on exact paths `PAIR_PATH`/`INFO_PATH` (586-587); every other path is unlimited. A page load of `/`, `/app.js` etc. is therefore not rate-limited and counts only against the 4-slot unauthenticated pool (`MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` 568; accept loop 696-706) until an authenticated reply moves the connection to the paired pool (843-858). A browser opens several connections at once (page plus assets plus keep-alive); the pool count is per TCP connection, with a 5 s handshake timeout (570) and 30 s idle (573). Moving to the paired pool is decided by `reply.authenticated`.
21	  - Everything goes over the frame: `requests.try_send` to the frame, replies after the frame's next pass (about one frame interval, per Spike 22). Static assets would take the same trip unless answered on the connection thread; the issue does not say which.
22	  - Certificate: `make_identity` 95, `tls_config` 144. No SAN list is inspected here; whether the cert covers the LAN IP the QR carries is not checked (see questions).
23	- `src/app.rs`
24	  - `serve_remote` 3017: line 3023 `strip_prefix("/api/v1/")` else 404 `not_found` via `refuse`. `GET /` and static paths are decided here (or in the adapter). Then `info`/`pair` unauthenticated (3028-3029); everything else `authenticate`s (3127) from `request.bearer` only.
25	  - `remote_info` 3568: JSON with `server_id`, `server_name`, `spki_sha256`, `capabilities`, `limits`, `pairing_open`. It has no `epoch`/`revision` in the body itself (wrapped by `envelope`). The page needs the key from here.
26	  - `remote_pair` 3606: checks window open, then body `spki_sha256` == host key (else `wrong_key`, counted as a failure), then code (case-insensitive), `device_name` default "Device". Returns `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}` in the JSON body through `envelope`. A cookie would need `RemoteReply` to carry headers (`RemoteReply` 389-393 is status, body, authenticated). Note: `wrong_key` counts against the three-failure budget, so a page that posts first and compares second would burn the window; the issue already orders compare first.
27	  - `remote_subscribe` 2723: requires `request.upgrade` and the already-authenticated device; WebSocket path is `/api/v1/events` (also `?scope=all`).
28	  - Command: `remote_command` 3159 (`POST /sessions/{id}/send` with body `op`; needs `control`); `refuse` 3754.
29	  - The `/api/v1/` allowlist in `serve_remote` (3027-3135) includes `projects`, `projects/{id}/sessions`, `sessions/{id}`, `waiting`, `sessions/{id}/screen`, `last-response`. Those are the reads the first cut needs; no new endpoint is evidently needed. Whether a "sessions grouped by project" load needs N+1 requests (`projects`, then each `projects/{id}/sessions`) or `waiting` plus per-project lists is a plan matter; the 8-per-pass drain and the 64-deep inbox bound a burst.
30	- `src/ui/remote.rs` pairing window 140-220: builds the QR `payload` as JSON (`server_id`, `spki_sha256`, `code`, `addresses` as `["ip:port"]`, 160-166) from `remote::local_address()` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:962`) and `cx.remote_port`; `qr_texture` 280; "Copy invite" at 203-206 copies the same string; `short_hash` and `spaced` helpers. Address may be empty (loopback), in which case the URL has no host.
31	- `src/core/remote.rs` (176 lines): identity, devices, `PairingWindow`, `new_device`.
32	- Swift: `PairingInvite` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:94-117`) decodes only JSON with `server_id`, `spki_sha256`, `code`, `addresses`; `parse` is `Wire.decode`. Used by `switchboard-remote pair` (`client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift:106-130`, one argument = invite text; three arguments = host, code, key), the browser view (`client/Sources/SwitchboardUI/BrowserView.swift:106`, `:883`) and `ConnectionManager.swift:474,482`. A URL form needs `parse` to accept it; `server_id` becomes the `id` param. `FixturesTests.swift` and the fixtures in `client/Fixtures` exist; `tests/remote.rs:1829` `the_client_fixtures_decode_on_both_sides`, `write_fixtures` 1587.
33	- Tests: `tests/remote.rs` (3592 lines), helpers `get` 327, `pair` 406; allowlist test `the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect` 682 asserts what non-`/api/v1/` paths do today (a new static route will change it); `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired` 426; pair rate limit 1406; stalled strangers 3226. There is no `web/` directory yet and no `include_str!` of text assets (only `include_bytes!` for icon and fonts, `src/main.rs:167`, `src/ui/theme.rs:203`).
34	- Docs to amend: `docs/remote-client.md` §4.1 bounds, §4.3 table (new GET paths), §5 (the "before anything but /info and /pair" line, token "never in a URL", QR payload), §9; `docs/design.md` remote status section (3107 on); README Layout table (`src/adapters/remote.rs` line 383, `src/ui/remote.rs` 423, new `web/` entry), `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased line.
35	
36	## Things the tree says that bear on the decisions
37

1	# Facts for issue #230 (web control surface)
2	
3	No spike was run: every open question left is a real-browser or real-device question, which cannot run here (no iPhone, no Safari with a LAN bind). Git status is clean.
4	
5	## Settled
6	
7	### The tree
8	
9	- The certificate has **no subjectAltName**: `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())` and only a CommonName `Switchboard <server_id>`. `src/adapters/remote.rs:95-120` (`make_identity`). Not for the LAN IP or any hostname.
10	- `respond` writes only `Content-Type: application/json`, `Content-Length`, `Connection`; the status reason table has no 302/304/405-other. `respond_upgrade` writes the 101 by hand with no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, so a subprotocol echo is a one-line additive change. `src/adapters/remote.rs:519-553`.
11	- `read_request` drops `cookie`, `user-agent`, `origin`, `host`, `sec-websocket-protocol`; `RemoteRequest` (360-372) and `RemoteReply` (389-393: status, body, authenticated) have no header fields. Cookie auth, a user-agent device name, a `Set-Cookie` on the pair reply, or static-file headers each need additive fields. (Investigation notes 18-19, 26.)
12	- Rate windows key on exact `PAIR_PATH`/`INFO_PATH` only (`Limits::limited`, 633-640); static paths are unlimited and count only against the 4-slot unauthenticated pool (568, 696-706) until a reply with `authenticated` promotes the connection (843-858).
13	- `serve_remote` refuses anything without the `/api/v1/` prefix as 404 `not_found` (`src/app.rs:3023`). `tests/remote.rs:682` (`the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else...`) only exercises `/api/v1/...` paths, so a new `GET /` does not break it. No test in `tests/remote.rs` or `src/adapters/remote.rs` uses a bare `/` path or `HEAD`/`OPTIONS` (grep). The plan must define HEAD/OPTIONS/trailing slash for the new routes; today they fall to 404.
14	- Revocation: a removed device's next request is 401 `unauthorized` "the token is not known; pair again" (`src/app.rs:3145`). Key rotation deletes all device records (`docs/remote-client.md` §5, line 315), so a stale token after rotation gives the same 401. Only `/info` (unauthenticated, carries `spki_sha256`/`server_id`) tells them apart: the page must compare `/info` after a 401 to say "identity changed" versus "revoked". Spec line 315/317: client shows "identity changed, pair again" and sends nothing.
15	- Events: metadata kinds `project`, `space`, `set`, `session` and collections `projects`, `sessions` (id = project), `waiting`, etc. arrive on `/api/v1/events` with **no `watch` frame**; `watch`/`unwatch` is only for content kinds `conversation`, `screen`, `run_output`, `file`. `docs/remote-client.md:240,256`. So "a session starts waiting and moves to top" needs only `changed {waiting}` / `changed {session}` plus a refetch of `waiting`; the last response needs `watch {conversation}` (it is a projection of that key, line 207), and the screen needs `watch {screen}`. A visible content view also refetches every 30 s (line 256). `scope=all` only adds Dispatch worker records (`src/app.rs:246-272`).
16	- `last_message` (the card's one-line excerpt) is a field of the session's metadata and moves with `changed {session}`, not with `conversation` (spec line 207).
17	- Only Claude Code sessions have a conversation; other kinds answer "no conversation" and the client falls back to `screen` (line 206): the issue's "last response or screen" split is the API's own.
18	- The QR payload is built in `src/ui/remote.rs:160-166` from `remote::local_address()` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:962`); the address may be empty (loopback). `PairingInvite.parse` in Swift is `Wire.decode` of JSON only (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift:94-117`).
19	- The code is Crockford, the key is hex, the id a UUID: none needs percent-decoding, so `read_request`'s undecoded query holds (`RemoteRequest::query` doc). `refuse` logs the path without the query.
20	
21	### Outside the tree
22	
23	**1. A WebSocket handshake to a host reached through a self-signed certificate is not reliable in Safari on iOS/iPadOS/Apple-silicon macOS even after the user clicks through.**
24	Cockpit's own docs: Safari's default WebSocket framework on iOS, iPadOS and ARM Macs does not support `wss://` with a self-signed or invalid certificate even when marked trusted; the workaround it ships is Settings > Safari > Advanced > Experimental Features > "NSURLSession WebSocket", or a valid certificate. https://cockpit-project.org/running/safari . Corroborated by WebKit bug 41419 (open since 2010: Safari honours the HTTPS click-through but not for `wss://`) https://www2.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=41419 . Two agreeing sources, no contradiction found; the Cockpit page names no iOS version, so the evidence covers "as of the page's current text, checked 2026-10-22". Consequence: the page needs a non-WebSocket fallback on Safari (poll `/api/v1/waiting` etc. on an interval, or `changed` by long poll); the WebSocket cannot be the only live path for the iPhone case in the acceptance text.
25	Queries: "WebSocket cookie sent on upgrade request SameSite Strict HttpOnly Secure self-signed certificate Safari Chrome"; "Safari iOS self-signed certificate visit this website Secure cookies not stored WebSocket wss fails after accepting certificate".
26	
27	**2. A browser fails a WebSocket whose 101 does not acknowledge a subprotocol the page offered.**
28	WHATWG WebSockets standard: if the client offered subprotocols and the response's `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` is absent/not one offered, fail the connection (stricter than RFC 6455, which lets the server omit it). https://websockets.spec.whatwg.org/ . Chrome reports match (Adobe/Lawouach threads, leads only). So a subprotocol token design must echo exactly one offered value in `respond_upgrade`; the standard's token grammar admits base64url/hex.
29	Queries: "RFC 6455 Sec-WebSocket-Protocol server must echo subprotocol browser fails connection if missing".
30	
31	**3. CSP `connect-src 'self'` does not cover same-host `wss:` in all browsers (Safari/WebKit).**
32	MDN note citing w3c/webappsec-csp#7: "`connect-src 'self'` does not resolve to websocket schemes in all browsers" https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Content-Security-Policy/connect-src ; WebKit bug 201591 (service worker, Safari ≤14 unfixed) https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=201591 . Two agreeing sources. Build to `connect-src 'self' wss:` (MDN's own example form); this adds no external host because the page is served by a host that is also the only wss target.
33	Query: "Content-Security-Policy connect-src 'self' does not match wss WebSocket Safari".
34	
35	**4. Safari has dropped `SameSite=Strict` cookies on WebSocket upgrades, and one report has `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` cookies not sent on a Safari WebSocket while Chrome/Firefox send them.**
36	WebKit bug 232666 (Strict cookies not sent on WebSocket in restored tabs, Safari 14/15, believed fixed 15.1) https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=232666 ; Apple forum thread 104488 (HttpOnly removal made Safari work; no version, no reply) https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/104488 . The second is a lead (single forum post) and unresolved; the first is a vendor bug that is reportedly fixed. Together with fact 1 this settles only that **cookie-on-upgrade in Safari is an observed risk with no vendor statement it is safe**; it does not settle the current behaviour (see Unresolved U1).
37	Query: same as fact 1.
38	
39	**5. Chrome ≥58 matches the host only against the SAN, never the CommonName.**
40	Forum agreement (Graylog, NethServer, TrueNAS, Palo Alto) and WebKit bug 158345 (Chrome and Safari would not accept a self-signed cert without a SAN) https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=158345 ; Cendio bug 7401 (iOS 13 needs SAN, EKU, validity under 3 years) https://bugzilla.cendio.com/show_bug.cgi?id=7401 . The current cert has no SAN (above) and a year-4096 validity, so a browser reaching it by IP gets a name-mismatch error, and per one Palo Alto article Chrome may not offer "Proceed" for a missing SAN (other users report it does; not settled). iOS 13+ also rejects validity over ~825 days for non-root trust (Cendio). Build to: the identity gains a SAN for the address the URL carries, which means the certificate is re-made on address change or the SAN lists every private interface address plus the Bonjour `.local` name; this changes `identity.json`'s certificate and thus the pinned SPKI only if the key is regenerated (it need not be: the SPKI is of the key).
41	Queries: "Chrome self-signed certificate without subjectAltName ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID IP address URL proceed anyway allowed".
42	
43	**6. iOS Camera opens a QR's web link in Safari from a notification banner showing the URL (iOS 11+).** https://www.iclarified.com/60903/ios-11-camera-app-recognizes-qr-codes/amp , https://thehackernews.com/2018/03/ios-qr-code-camera.html (hostname-parsing flaw with crafted `@`/port text; our URL has neither `@` nor userinfo). Nothing found on IP-literal hosts, ports or self-signed hosts being refused before Safari; the Camera hands the URL to Safari, which then shows the certificate page. Queries: "iPhone Camera app QR code https URL IP address port self-signed certificate opens Safari notification". Android is not covered.
44	
45	## Unresolved
46	
47	**U1. Does current Safari (iOS 26-class, macOS 26-class) carry a `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` cookie, set by a fetch response on a click-through page, on `fetch` and on `new WebSocket()`?**
48	Tried: the three searches under facts 1 and 4 plus fetching the Apple thread; found only 2021-era and undated reports. Why not settled: no source states current behaviour. Line to build to: **favourable** (cookie works): the plan may use the cookie for `fetch` and WebSocket. **Unfavourable**: the plan must still keep the bearer header for native clients, send the token for the page's `fetch` in an `Authorization` header from memory/`sessionStorage`, and use the `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` token (echoing it) or authenticate the first WebSocket frame; it must also carry the polling fallback of fact 1. The plan should build the WebSocket path so one transport (subprotocol or first-frame auth) works without cookies, and treat a cookie as an addition only if the owner confirms it (O1).
49	
50	**U2. Whether an iOS Safari click-through exception covers `fetch` from the page and persists (how long).** Tried: same queries; Cockpit says the HTTPS page works after trust but WebSocket does not. No source gives the duration. Build to: the page treats a failed `fetch` with no HTTP status as "unreachable or certificate not trusted" and says so; it never assumes the exception outlives a session. Favourable: nothing extra. Unfavourable: the pairing window's text names the warning as repeating.
51	
52	**U3. Whether Chrome/Android offers "Proceed" for a certificate with no SAN, and whether Android camera/Lens opens an IP:port https URL.** Tried: query under fact 5 and 6; sources disagree or are silent. Build to: add the SAN regardless (fact 5); that makes the Chrome case equal to the ordinary self-signed case.
53	
54	**U4. Whether a Firefox/Chrome page whose query was removed by `history.replaceState` before any request still has the code in the browser history or the camera app's own history.** The camera app and the first `GET /?code=...` request exist before the script runs, so the code reaches the host once and may sit in the camera app's or the OS's history. Not settleable by search. Build to: the code is single-use and the window closes after the pair (spec §5), so a leaked URL is dead after pairing and after five minutes; the plan says so in the dialog and does not claim more.

If the owner reports the cookie works, the plan may swap `sessionStorage` for the HttpOnly cookie; if the socket works, the poll becomes a fallback only.

Do any of the owner's networks isolate wifi clients, or does the phone's camera app refuse the URL (and what does its banner show)?** Works in both cases: the page and the pairing window's text assume nothing about reachability beyond "the same network"; an unreachable host shows the unreachable state of U2.

  - **file content**: the file is read whole under its limit, masked, then sent.
  - **last response** and the card excerpt: masked from the turn's full text, then cut.
  The secret set for a session is the project's secret variables plus its granted sets; for a file it is the owning project's. The set is resolved **before any cached content is returned**, on every read, and its **policy fingerprint** (a hash over the sorted names and values, held in memory only, never logged or stored) is part of every masked cache's version (§4.4): a new grant, a changed value 

New read models, added to the wire crate:

- `session.conversation`: the `Conversation` from `ports::transcript` as a wire shape: title, model, branch, usage, and turns paged by **turn number** (`n`, 1-based). The host parses the whole JSONL, as the session view does, from the app-level cache (§4.4); a transcript the app can show is one the port can serve, and the supported size is whatever the app handles, which the spike measures. What p
- `session.last_response`: the last turn's `final_text`, its `n` and `end`. It is a **projection of the `conversation` key**: it is read from the same cache, carries the conversation's content revision, is watched by watching `conversation`, and refreshes on `changed {conversation}`; a window showing only the last response registers that watch. The compact card's one-line excerpt is not part of it
- `session.runs`: a command's or service's runs as the record holds them (`Run`: `n`, started, ended, exit, artifacts' names, not their paths). `session.run_output`: the tail of one run's scrollback log (`scrollback::tail_text`, escapes stripped, `lines` clamped to 500), redacted; a run whose log was pruned or rotated answers with that reason. This is how an exited command whose pane is gone is st
- `file.read`: content of a file **only if some working set pins it** (`PinTarget::File` with that project and path). The read goes through a new `ports::files` method, `read_pinned(root, relative)`, not through the UI's preview loader. Confinement is by descriptors, not by path strings, so it stays valid while names change under it:
  - the relative path is rejected if it is absolute, empty, or has a `..` or `.` component, before anything touches the disk (a persisted pin can hold anything);

# Plan: issue #230, a web control surface on the remote port

One commit. The app runs at every step. Every line number below was
checked in this worktree on 2026-10-22; the facts file is cited as
"facts" with its own numbering (Settled 1-6, Unresolved U1-U4, owner
O1-O3).

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"Accept the certificate warning, see the sessions" does not work
  with today's certificate.** `make_identity` builds
  `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())` with a CommonName only
  (`src/adapters/remote.rs:102-106`): no subjectAltName, no extended key
  usage, validity to year 4096. A browser matches an IP-literal URL
  against the SAN, so the QR's `https://<ip>:<port>/` is a name
  mismatch before any click-through (facts, Settled 5). The plan
  re-issues the certificate over the same key with SANs (step 2), so
  the pinned SPKI and every paired native device are untouched.
- **The WebSocket cannot be the page's only live path.** The issue
  treats the events socket as the live channel. Safari on iOS, iPadOS
  and Apple-silicon Macs does not complete `wss://` to a self-signed
  host even after the click-through (facts, Settled 1). The page's base
  is a poll of the same REST reads; the socket, when it opens, only
  makes the refetch immediate.
- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" gets three exceptions, and
  they are answered on the connection thread**, not in `serve_remote`.
  `src/app.rs:3023` (`strip_prefix("/api/v1/")` else 404) is
  unchanged. The pages are constants; sending them through the frame
  would spend the 64-deep inbox and a frame pass per file for no state.
- **The card's one-line excerpt is not on the wire.** The issue lists it
  on each row. `docs/remote-client.md:207` says it is `last_message`, "a
  field of the session's metadata", but `SessionView`
  (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has no such field and `SessionRecord`
  has none (`last_message` exists only as the Stop hook event's payload,
  `src/ports/events.rs:24`). The card builds its excerpt in the UI from
  the parsed conversation (`agent_excerpt`, `src/ui/cards.rs:558`). The
  plan's rows show name, kind, the `card` word and `waiting_reason`; the
  excerpt (first line of the last response) appears in the session view
  only. Putting an `excerpt` on `SessionView` is a follow-up. The plan
  also corrects the spec sentence at `:207`.
- **No endpoint tells a device its scope.** The issue wants the scope in
  the header and the reply box hidden without `control`. `/pair`'s
  reply carries it once, but with the token in an HttpOnly cookie the
  script never sees that reply's token and, after a reload, nothing at
  all. The page cannot do without one read, so the plan adds
  `GET /api/v1/device` (step 5). It is also the page's "am I still
  paired" probe.
- **The device name comes from the page, not the host.** The host
  drops `user-agent` today. `/pair` already takes `device_name`
  (`src/app.rs:3641`); the page sends "Safari on iPhone" from
  `navigator.userAgent`. No header capture, no record change.
- **The cookie cannot rest on `SameSite=Strict` alone.** Cookies are
  scoped by host, not port, and "same site" ignores the port. Another
  service on the same address, or a second Switchboard on another port,
  is same-site, and nothing in the tree consults `Origin` (`read_request`
  drops it). The plan adds an `Origin` check for cookie-authenticated
  writes and upgrades, and a per-installation cookie name.
- **"Sessions grouped by project" is not N+1 fetches on load.** Rows come
  from `waiting` first; a project's group fetches
  `projects/{id}/sessions` when it is expanded (groups with a waiting
  session start expanded). This keeps a first load within the paired
  pool and the 8-per-pass drain.
- **`history.replaceState` before anything else does not keep the code
  from the host or the camera app.** The first `GET /?code=…` has
  already crossed the wire and the camera app may keep the URL (facts,
  U4). The plan does not claim more than the single-use code gives: it
  is dead after one pairing, five minutes or three wrong tries
  (`docs/remote-client.md` §5), and the dialog says so.

## The decisions the issue asks for

**1. Browser trust: the click-through is the trust step.** The host does
not offer its certificate for download. Reasons: iOS makes the owner
install a profile and then enable full trust in Settings, a flow longer
than the one it replaces; it needs a new pre-pairing endpoint that §5's
rule ("nothing before pairing but `/info` and `/pair`") would have to
admit; and a trusted certificate does not fix Safari's `wss://` anyway
(facts, Settled 1, "even when marked trusted"). What the click-through
buys: an encrypted channel to whoever answered at that address. What it
does not buy: the `key` in the URL lets a genuine page refuse to send
the code to a host whose `/info` key differs, but a page served by an
impostor is not a genuine page, and an impostor that relays the page's
own `/info` and `/pair` calls to the real host passes the host's
`spki_sha256` check, because the browser cannot pin. The trust root is
therefore the QR on the owner's own screen plus the five-minute,
single-use, three-try window, and the browser path is weaker than the
native pin. The pairing window says so in a line (UI below) and keeps
`read` the default scope. The decision this plan does not take: whether
the owner wants browser pairing to grant `control` at all; it is the
existing radio.

§5's rule becomes: a non-loopback bind serves `/info`, `/pair` and the
three page files before pairing, nothing else. The page holds no
secret and no host state.

**2. The token reaches the socket by the cookie, and only by the cookie.**
`/pair` with a body field `delivery: "cookie"` omits `token` from its
reply and sets `__Host-sb-<first 8 hex of server_id>=<token>; Path=/;
Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`. `fetch` and the
WebSocket upgrade both carry it, the script never reads it, and nothing
is in `localStorage` but the public pin. The cookie name is per
installation (the `__Host-` prefix forces `Secure`, `Path=/`, no
`Domain`), so two Switchboards on one address do not overwrite each
other. The native clients keep the bearer header and the `token` in the
reply; a request with a bearer never consults the cookie. No
`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` token, no first-frame token and no
`sessionStorage` copy: a script-readable store is the weaker place for a
credential and the plan builds one transport.

Whether Safari carries that cookie is Unresolved U1 (facts), so it is
the first thing the implementer tests (step 1), and it splits cleanly:
- *`fetch` carries it* (the ordinary case, and what the page needs for
  its base behaviour, the poll): build on.
- *The WebSocket upgrade does not carry it*: the socket answers 401, the
  page stays on the poll. Nothing breaks, because the poll is already
  the base. This is the answer on iOS whichever way U1 falls.
- *`fetch` does not carry it on Safari*: stop, record it in the spike
  README, and report to the owner. The fallback (a token the script
  holds, sent as `Authorization`) is a follow-up for the owner (O1), not
  a second transport built now.

**3. One QR.** The QR and "Copy invite" carry the URL
`https://<address>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
The JSON form is no longer produced. The Swift `PairingInvite.parse`
accepts both (a pasted old invite still works) and the URL form fills
`addresses` from the host and port. No camera client needs the JSON.
An empty address (no network) gives `127.0.0.1`, which the certificate
covers, so the same Mac can pair its own browser.

**4. Static paths.**
- Exactly `GET` or `HEAD` on `/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css`; any query is
  ignored (so `/?code=` serves the same page). Other methods on those
  paths: 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD`. Every other path, including
  `/index.html`, `//` and `/favicon.ico`, falls through to the frame and
  its 404 as today.
- Headers on all three: `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`,
  `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, `text/css; charset=utf-8`;
  `Cache-Control: no-store` (the page is 20 KB, and an old script
  against a newer API is the worse failure); `X-Content-Type-Options:
  nosniff`; `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; and on the HTML,
  `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
  style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' wss:; img-src data:; base-uri
  'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src
  'self' wss:` rather than `'self'` because WebKit does not resolve
  `'self'` to `wss:` (facts, Settled 3). That sentence in the facts says
  `wss:` adds no external host; it permits any secure socket, but only
  from the one fixed script, which has no injection point (no inline
  script, no `innerHTML`). The page's `<link rel=icon href="data:,">`
  stops the favicon request.
- Pool and rate: the three files are answered on the connection thread,
  a millisecond each, on the same connection a browser then uses for its
  first authenticated `fetch`, which promotes it to the paired pool
  (`src/adapters/remote.rs:843-858`). They count against the 4-slot
  unauthenticated pool at accept like `/info`, and a new window `pages`
  in `Limits` (`:623`), 120 per minute per listener (a load is 3
  requests), answers 429 past it. An unpaired browser's load therefore
  cannot reach the frame at all.
- Opened with no code and no token the page shows the host's name (from
  `/info`) and "Open Remote devices on the Mac, allow pairing, and scan
  its QR code."

**5. Where the page lives.** `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`,
`web/app.css`, embedded with `include_str!` by a new
`src/adapters/remote_page.rs` (the routing table, the headers, a pure
`route(method, path) -> Option<Page>`). No bundler, no dependency. Tests
in "Tests" below.

**6. The device record.** A browser is a `PairedDevice` like any other,
listed and revocable in the Remote devices dialog (unchanged). Revoking
it deletes the record, so its next request is 401 and the host clears
the cookie in that refusal.

## The record

Nothing new is stored on the host. `identity.json`, `devices.json` and
`PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`) are unchanged: the cookie
holds the same token whose SHA-256 the device record already has
(`token_sha256`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:345`), looked up by
`core.device_by_token` (`src/app.rs:3127`). The certificate in
`identity.json` stays as written; the browser's certificate is made in
memory (step 2), so `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`src/ports/remote.rs:17`,
1 today) and `SCHEMA_VERSION` (`src/core/model.rs:12`, 16 today) do not
move. If the implementer finds a field has to be added after all, the
bump is: the value in `model.rs` or `ports/remote.rs` at implementation
time, plus one, with a step in `adapters::store::migrate`.

The page's own record lives on the device, not on the host: the pin
`{server_id, spki_sha256}` it last paired with, in `localStorage` under
try/catch (public values, so a script-readable store is fine), used only
to say "identity changed" versus "revoked". The page renders with
nothing in it.

## The signals

- `changed`/`removed`/`resync_required` are the existing frames; no new
  event, no new revision rule. The page applies §4.4 as the headset
  does: it keeps one held revision per key (`waiting`, `projects`,
  `sessions:<project>`, `session:<id>`, `conversation:<id>`,
  `screen:<id>`), applies a reply only if its envelope `revision` is at
  or past the held one, and on `epoch` change or `resync_required`
  refetches everything.
- **Live path.** Base: a timer refetches `waiting`, every expanded
  project's sessions and the open session's content, every 5 s (3 s when
  the open session is waiting). When the socket opens and `hello` lands,
  the timer relaxes to 30 s (the spec's own visible-view refetch,
  `docs/remote-client.md:256`) and `changed {waiting}`,
  `{sessions,id}`, `{session,id}` and the watched content kinds trigger
  the matching refetch at once. Metadata kinds need no `watch` frame; the
  open session sends `watch {conversation|screen, id}` and `unwatch` on
  leaving (`docs/remote-client.md:240,256`). "A session that starts
  waiting moves to the top without a reload" is `changed {waiting}` then
  a `waiting` refetch on the socket, and the next poll without it.
- **Failure words**, each one sentence in the page: a `fetch` that fails
  with no HTTP status is "The host is unreachable, or this browser does
  not trust its certificate" (facts, U2: the page never assumes the
  click-through outlives the session); a 401 on `/device` triggers
  `/info`, and a different `spki_sha256` or `server_id` from the pin is
  "Identity changed, pair again" (nothing more is sent), the same key
  with a pin stored is "This device was revoked", and no pin is the
  no-code screen; `pairing_closed`, `wrong_code` and `wrong_key` from
  `/pair` are worded plainly.

## The actions and effects

None in the core: no `AppAction`, no `Effect`, no change under
`src/core/`. The pairing window, the failure counter and `Paired`
already carry everything (`src/app.rs:3606-3665`). The work is in the
adapter and in `serve_remote`'s handlers, in this order:

1. **Spike first, `spikes/23-web-cookie/`.** CLAUDE.md requires one for a
   new risky mechanism. Do steps 2-5 minimally with a 20-line throwaway
   `web/` page that, on a `delivery: "cookie"` pair, does a `fetch` of
   `/device` and opens `new WebSocket` to `/api/v1/events`, and run it in
   Safari and Chrome on the Mac against a LAN bind (accept the warning).
   Record in the README: cookie stored, returned on `fetch`, returned on
   the upgrade, per browser and version. The owner repeats it on the
   iPhone (O1); the plan does not wait on that, the result only decides
   whether the socket ever opens there. If `fetch` fails in Safari, stop
   as in decision 2.
2. **Certificate with SANs, in memory.** Replace the single fixed cert in
   `tls_config` (`:144`, signature unchanged) with a `ResolvesServerCert`
   that holds one `CertifiedKey` and the address it was made for. On each
   handshake it compares `local_address()` (`:962`, a connected UDP
   socket, no packet sent) and re-makes the certificate over the same
   `rcgen::KeyPair::from_pem(key)` when the address moved. The
   certificate carries SANs `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and the
   current address, `ExtendedKeyUsage::ServerAuth`, the same CommonName,
   and a 397-day validity (facts, Settled 5: iOS 13+ limits). The key is
   the same, so `spki_sha256` is the same and `identity.json` is not
   rewritten; native clients ignore dates and names (`pinned_client`,
   `:168`). The Bonjour `.local` name is not added: the QR carries an IP.
3. **Request and reply fields** (additive, `src/adapters/remote.rs`).
   `RemoteRequest` (`:360`, one literal, in `read_request`) gains
   `cookies: Vec<(String, String)>` (only names starting `__Host-sb-`,
   so other sites' cookies never enter memory), `origin:
   Option<String>`, `host: Option<String>`. `RemoteReply` (`:389`)
   gains `set_cookie: Option<String>`; its ~11 literal sites in
   `src/app.rs` (lines 1664, 1679, 2365-2376, 2754, 3570, 3723, 3736,
   3767) and `:829` add `set_cookie: None`. `respond` (`:530`) becomes a
   thin call of a general writer taking content type, extra headers and
   a head-only flag; the status table gains nothing new.
4. **Pages on the connection thread.** In `connection` (`:770`), before
   `limited`, `remote_page::route` answers the three paths (decision 4).
   `HEAD` writes the headers with the real `Content-Length` and no body.
5. **Cookie auth, `/device`, `Origin`.** In `authenticate` (`:3127`):
   a bearer wins; otherwise the cookie named for this installation. A
   cookie-authenticated request that is not a plain `GET`, and every
   upgrade, must carry `Origin: https://<Host header>` or it is 403
   `forbidden_origin`, logged by code. An unknown cookie token is 401 as
   today, with `set_cookie` clearing the cookie (`Max-Age=0`).
   `remote_pair` (`:3606`) reads `delivery`; for `"cookie"` it omits
   `token` and sets the cookie on the reply. `serve_remote` (`:3017`)
   gains, beside `events` and after `authenticate`, `GET device` ->
   `{device_id, name, scope}` through `envelope` (any paired scope). The
   `Referrer-Policy` and the unchanged `refuse` log (path without query)
   keep the code out of the log.
6. **The invite URL.** A pure `remote::invite_url(address:
   Option<IpAddr>, port, server_id, key, code) -> String` in
   `src/adapters/remote.rs` beside `local_address`, using
   `SocketAddr::new(ip, port)` so an IPv6 address is bracketed. No
   percent-encoding: the code is Crockford, the key hex, the id a UUID
   (the undecoded query, facts, tree).
7. **Swift.** `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/
   Info.swift:112`) tries JSON, then a URL (`URLComponents`: `code`, `key`,
   `id`, host and port into `addresses`, a host with a colon rebracketed).
   `switchboard-remote pair` and `BrowserView` call `parse` and need no
   change. Run `swift test` in `client/` on the Mac (not run in
   planning).
8. **The page** (`web/`), plain DOM, `textContent` only (session names
   and agent output are untrusted; the last response is shown as
   `white-space: pre-wrap` text, not markdown). Sessions grouped by
   project, waiting first and marked in text as well as colour; the kind,
   the card word and `waiting_reason`; the session view shows the last
   response for a Claude Code session (falling back to `screen` on
   `no conversation`) and `screen` for every other kind; a reply box that
   posts `send` `{op: <uuid>, text}` only when `/device` says `control`;
   host name and scope in the header. A reply is submitted with a fresh
   `op` and, on a timeout, a status query (`GET ops/{op}`) and never a
   resend (`docs/remote-client.md` §4.5).

## The UI

`src/ui/remote.rs`, the pairing window (`:140-220`): `payload` becomes
`remote::invite_url(...)`; the QR, "Copy invite" and the "Address" line
follow. The window's help text (`:187-195`) gains, after the existing
sentence: "A browser pairs by this QR too: it will warn about the
certificate, which is expected for a host that signs its own. The
browser cannot check the host's key the way the apps do, so pair only
from this screen. The code works once." No new widget and no
`SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line: `pairing <code>` (`src/script.rs:730`)
already puts the window in this state. README's dev-aid list is
unchanged.

## The tests

- **`src/adapters/remote_page.rs` unit tests**: `route` for each path,
  `HEAD`, a `POST` (405 with `Allow`), `/index.html` and `//` (none).
- **Embedded page, `tests/remote.rs`**: `index.html` references only
  `/app.js`, `/app.css` and `data:`; no `<script>` body, no `style=`
  attribute, no `http(s)://` or `//host` URL anywhere in the three files;
  every `/api/v1/<first segment>` literal in `app.js` is in the set the
  host serves (`info`, `pair`, `device`, `projects`, `sessions`,
  `waiting`, `ops`, `events`).
- **The new paths over the real listener** (`call` at `:300` returns
  status and JSON only; add a sibling returning headers and raw body):
  200 unpaired for all three with the named `Content-Type`,
  `Cache-Control: no-store`, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, and the CSP on
  the HTML, containing no `unsafe-inline`; `HEAD` has no body and the
  right length; a query changes nothing; `/api/v1/*` allowlist test
  (`:682`) and `/info` test (`:426`) still pass untouched; the `pages`
  window answers 429 past 120.
- **The pairing flow end to end with the host's own client, as the CLI
  does** (no UI test drives a browser): take `invite_url`, parse its
  query, `GET /info` and compare `key` and `id`, `POST /pair` with
  `delivery: "cookie"` (reply has no `token`; `Set-Cookie` has `Secure`,
  `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, the `__Host-sb-` name), then
  with only the cookie: `GET /device` (scope), `GET /waiting`, `POST
  .../send` with the right `Origin` (control) and with a wrong one (403),
  `GET` of `events` upgrade with the right `Origin` (101, `hello`) and a
  wrong one (403); a bearer request is unchanged and a bearer wins over a
  wrong cookie; a read-scope device's `send` is 403 `scope`; revoke ->
  the next cookie request is 401 and the reply clears the cookie, and the
  subscriber is closed; key rotation -> 401 and `/info` shows the new key.
- **Certificate**: a rustls client with the stock webpki verifier and the
  presented certificate as its only anchor connects by `localhost`,
  `127.0.0.1` and the current `local_address()` (skips cleanly when there
  is no address), and `spki_sha256` is the same before and after a
  re-issue. If the webpki client will not take an end-entity anchor,
  fall back to parsing the SANs from the DER.
- **`invite_url`** unit test: IPv4, IPv6 (bracketed), no address.
- **`tests/ui.rs:7424`** (`remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`):
  the copied invite is now the URL; assert it starts `https://`, has the
  window's code, key and id, and no JSON.
- **Fixtures**: add `client/Fixtures/invite_url.txt`, written by
  `write_fixtures` (`tests/remote.rs:1587`) from `invite_url`, decoded by
  a new `FixturesTests.swift` case through `PairingInvite.parse`
  (extends `the_client_fixtures_decode_on_both_sides`, `:1829`). `/device`
  gets no fixture: no Swift speaker reads it.
- **Not testable here, said plainly**: the page's script runs in no test
  (no browser, no JS runner, and the plan adds neither). Its logic is
  checked by the acceptance steps below, run by hand in a real browser
  on a LAN bind, and kept to small pure functions.
- **Acceptance by hand**: `cargo run --locked`; Remote devices, LAN,
  allow pairing with `control`; scan on a phone, accept the warning,
  see sessions; a session that starts waiting moves up (on the poll if
  the socket does not open); send a reply and watch it arrive in the
  pane; revoke the phone and see "revoked" on its next refresh. Also
  open the same QR text in Safari and Chrome on the Mac.

## Docs, in the same commit

- `docs/remote-client.md`: §4.1 bounds (three page paths, the `pages`
  window, answered on the connection thread); §4.3 table (the three
  `GET` page paths and `GET /api/v1/device`); §5 (the pre-pairing line;
  the token sentence: bearer over the pinned connection **or** the
  host-set HttpOnly cookie for a browser, still never in a URL; the QR
  is the URL; the browser-trust paragraph from decision 1; the Origin
  rule); `:207` (the excerpt is not a `SessionView` field); §9 untouched.
- `docs/design.md`: a "Web control surface" item in the Remote client
  status section (from `:3107`), with the known gaps: no excerpt on the
  wire, Safari socket unreliable, browser pairing not pinned, U1 as
  measured in the spike.
- `README.md`: Layout table lines for `src/adapters/remote.rs` (`:383`),
  `src/ui/remote.rs` (`:423`), a new `src/adapters/remote_page.rs`, a
  new `web/` entry, and `spikes/23-web-cookie`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, under Unreleased: "A browser can pair and control the
  host from the pairing window's QR code."

## For the owner, after this lands

- O1: on the iPhone or iPad, state the iOS version, does the cookie
  return on `fetch` and on the socket? If `fetch` fails, a token held by
  the script is the follow-up; if the socket works, the poll relaxes to
  a fallback only.
- O2 and O3 (client isolation, the camera banner, Android "Proceed")
  change nothing in the plan; they only explain a phone that cannot
  reach the page.
- Follow-ups named, not built: an `excerpt` on `SessionView`; the
  certificate download if the owner prefers it to the click-through
  (it would change §5's pre-pairing rule); raising the 4-slot pool if the
  spike shows a browser's parallel connections being closed at accept.

## Commit message

`Serve a browser control page from the remote port, paired by a URL QR and an HttpOnly cookie`

## Contract additions

- `RemoteRequest`: `cookies: Vec<(String, String)>`, `origin:
  Option<String>`, `host: Option<String>`.
- `RemoteReply`: `set_cookie: Option<String>`.
- `POST /api/v1/pair`: optional body field `delivery` (`"cookie"`); with
  it the reply omits `token` and sets the `__Host-sb-<id8>` cookie.
- `GET /api/v1/device` -> `{device_id, name, scope}`, any paired scope.
- Cookie authentication for every `/api/v1/` endpoint, with the
  `Origin` rule for non-`GET` requests and upgrades; error code
  `forbidden_origin` (403).
- Unauthenticated `GET`/`HEAD` of `/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css`; `Limits`
  gains a `pages` window (120 a minute); new module
  `src/adapters/remote_page.rs`; new directory `web/`.
- `remote::invite_url`; the pairing QR and "Copy invite" now carry the
  URL (`PairingInvite.parse` accepts the URL and the JSON).
- `tls_config` serves a certificate re-issued over the same key with
  SANs and a 397-day validity; `spki_sha256` and `identity.json` are
  unchanged.
- No change to `model.rs`, `AppAction`, `Effect`, `src/ports/`, or

# Plan: issue #230, a web control surface on the remote port

One commit. The app runs at every step. Every line number below was
checked in this worktree on 2026-10-22; the facts file is cited as
"facts" with its own numbering (Settled 1-6, Unresolved U1-U4, owner
O1-O3).

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"Accept the certificate warning, see the sessions" does not work
  with today's certificate.** `make_identity` builds
  `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())` with a CommonName only
  (`src/adapters/remote.rs:102-106`): no subjectAltName, no extended key
  usage, validity to year 4096. A browser matches an IP-literal URL
  against the SAN, so the QR's `https://<ip>:<port>/` is a name
  mismatch before any click-through (facts, Settled 5). The plan
  re-issues the certificate over the same key with SANs (step 2), so
  the pinned SPKI and every paired native device are untouched.
- **The WebSocket cannot be the page's only live path.** The issue
  treats the events socket as the live channel. Safari on iOS, iPadOS
  and Apple-silicon Macs does not complete `wss://` to a self-signed
  host even after the click-through (facts, Settled 1). The page's base
  is a poll of the same REST reads; the socket, when it opens, only
  makes the refetch immediate.
- **"Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused" gets three exceptions, and
  they are answered on the connection thread**, not in `serve_remote`.
  `src/app.rs:3023` (`strip_prefix("/api/v1/")` else 404) is
  unchanged. The pages are constants; sending them through the frame
  would spend the 64-deep inbox and a frame pass per file for no state.
- **The card's one-line excerpt is not on the wire.** The issue lists it
  on each row. `docs/remote-client.md:207` says it is `last_message`, "a
  field of the session's metadata", but `SessionView`
  (`control/src/lib.rs:637-688`) has no such field and `SessionRecord`
  has none (`last_message` exists only as the Stop hook event's payload,
  `src/ports/events.rs:24`). The card builds its excerpt in the UI from
  the parsed conversation (`agent_excerpt`, `src/ui/cards.rs:558`). The
  plan's rows show name, kind, the `card` word and `waiting_reason`; the
  excerpt (first line of the last response) appears in the session view
  only. Putting an `excerpt` on `SessionView` is a follow-up. The plan
  also corrects the spec sentence at `:207`.
- **No endpoint tells a device its scope.** The issue wants the scope in
  the header and the reply box hidden without `control`. `/pair`'s
  reply carries it once, but with the token in an HttpOnly cookie the
  script never sees that reply's token and, after a reload, nothing at
  all. The page cannot do without one read, so the plan adds
  `GET /api/v1/device` (step 5). It is also the page's "am I still
  paired" probe.
- **The device name comes from the page, not the host.** The host
  drops `user-agent` today. `/pair` already takes `device_name`
  (`src/app.rs:3641`); the page sends "Safari on iPhone" from
  `navigator.userAgent`. No header capture, no record change.
- **The cookie cannot rest on `SameSite=Strict` alone.** Cookies are
  scoped by host, not port, and "same site" ignores the port. Another
  service on the same address, or a second Switchboard on another port,
  is same-site, and nothing in the tree consults `Origin` (`read_request`
  drops it). The plan adds an `Origin` check for cookie-authenticated
  writes and upgrades, and a per-installation cookie name.
- **"Sessions grouped by project" is not N+1 fetches on load.** Rows come
  from `waiting` first; a project's group fetches
  `projects/{id}/sessions` when it is expanded (groups with a waiting
  session start expanded). This keeps a first load within the paired
  pool and the 8-per-pass drain.
- **`history.replaceState` before anything else does not keep the code
  from the host or the camera app.** The first `GET /?code=…` has
  already crossed the wire and the camera app may keep the URL (facts,
  U4). The plan does not claim more than the single-use code gives: it
  is dead after one pairing, five minutes or three wrong tries
  (`docs/remote-client.md` §5), and the dialog says so.

## The decisions the issue asks for

**1. Browser trust: the click-through is the trust step.** The host does
not offer its certificate for download. Reasons: iOS makes the owner
install a profile and then enable full trust in Settings, a flow longer
than the one it replaces; it needs a new pre-pairing endpoint that §5's
rule ("nothing before pairing but `/info` and `/pair`") would have to
admit; and a trusted certificate does not fix Safari's `wss://` anyway
(facts, Settled 1, "even when marked trusted"). What the click-through
buys: an encrypted channel to whoever answered at that address. What it
does not buy: the `key` in the URL lets a genuine page refuse to send
the code to a host whose `/info` key differs, but a page served by an
impostor is not a genuine page, and an impostor that relays the page's
own `/info` and `/pair` calls to the real host passes the host's
`spki_sha256` check, because the browser cannot pin. The trust root is
therefore the QR on the owner's own screen plus the five-minute,
single-use, three-try window, and the browser path is weaker than the
native pin. The pairing window says so in a line (UI below) and keeps
`read` the default scope. The decision this plan does not take: whether
the owner wants browser pairing to grant `control` at all; it is the
existing radio.

§5's rule becomes: a non-loopback bind serves `/info`, `/pair` and the
three page files before pairing, nothing else. The page holds no
secret and no host state.

**2. The token reaches the socket by the cookie, and only by the cookie.**
`/pair` with a body field `delivery: "cookie"` omits `token` from its
reply and sets `__Host-sb-<first 8 hex of server_id>=<token>; Path=/;
Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=34560000`. `fetch` and the
WebSocket upgrade both carry it, the script never reads it, and nothing
is in `localStorage` but the public pin. The cookie name is per
installation (the `__Host-` prefix forces `Secure`, `Path=/`, no
`Domain`), so two Switchboards on one address do not overwrite each
other. The native clients keep the bearer header and the `token` in the
reply; a request with a bearer never consults the cookie. No
`Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` token, no first-frame token and no
`sessionStorage` copy: a script-readable store is the weaker place for a
credential and the plan builds one transport.

Whether Safari carries that cookie is Unresolved U1 (facts), so it is
the first thing the implementer tests (step 1), and it splits cleanly:
- *`fetch` carries it* (the ordinary case, and what the page needs for
  its base behaviour, the poll): build on.
- *The WebSocket upgrade does not carry it*: the socket answers 401, the
  page stays on the poll. Nothing breaks, because the poll is already
  the base. This is the answer on iOS whichever way U1 falls.
- *`fetch` does not carry it on Safari*: stop, record it in the spike
  README, and report to the owner. The fallback (a token the script
  holds, sent as `Authorization`) is a follow-up for the owner (O1), not
  a second transport built now.

**3. One QR.** The QR and "Copy invite" carry the URL
`https://<address>:<port>/?code=<code>&key=<spki_sha256>&id=<server_id>`.
The JSON form is no longer produced. The Swift `PairingInvite.parse`
accepts both (a pasted old invite still works) and the URL form fills
`addresses` from the host and port. No camera client needs the JSON.
An empty address (no network) gives `127.0.0.1`, which the certificate
covers, so the same Mac can pair its own browser.

**4. Static paths.**
- Exactly `GET` or `HEAD` on `/`, `/app.js`, `/app.css`; any query is
  ignored (so `/?code=` serves the same page). Other methods on those
  paths: 405 with `Allow: GET, HEAD`. Every other path, including
  `/index.html`, `//` and `/favicon.ico`, falls through to the frame and
  its 404 as today.
- Headers on all three: `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`,
  `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, `text/css; charset=utf-8`;
  `Cache-Control: no-store` (the page is 20 KB, and an old script
  against a newer API is the worse failure); `X-Content-Type-Options:
  nosniff`; `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; and on the HTML,
  `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self';
  style-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' wss:; img-src data:; base-uri
  'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`. `connect-src
  'self' wss:` rather than `'self'` because WebKit does not resolve
  `'self'` to `wss:` (facts, Settled 3). That sentence in the facts says
  `wss:` adds no external host; it permits any secure socket, but only
  from the one fixed script, which has no injection point (no inline
  script, no `innerHTML`). The page's `<link rel=icon href="data:,">`
  stops the favicon request.
- Pool and rate: the three files are answered on the connection thread,
  a millisecond each, on the same connection a browser then uses for its
  first authenticated `fetch`, which promotes it to the paired pool
  (`src/adapters/remote.rs:843-858`). They count against the 4-slot
  unauthenticated pool at accept like `/info`, and a new window `pages`
  in `Limits` (`:623`), 120 per minute per listener (a load is 3
  requests), answers 429 past it. An unpaired browser's load therefore
  cannot reach the frame at all.
- Opened with no code and no token the page shows the host's name (from
  `/info`) and "Open Remote devices on the Mac, allow pairing, and scan
  its QR code."

**5. Where the page lives.** `web/index.html`, `web/app.js`,
`web/app.css`, embedded with `include_str!` by a new
`src/adapters/remote_page.rs` (the routing table, the headers, a pure
`route(method, path) -> Option<Page>`). No bundler, no dependency. Tests
in "Tests" below.

**6. The device record.** A browser is a `PairedDevice` like any other,
listed and revocable in the Remote devices dialog (unchanged). Revoking
it deletes the record, so its next request is 401 and the host clears
the cookie in that refusal.

## The record

Nothing new is stored on the host. `identity.json`, `devices.json` and
`PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`) are unchanged: the cookie
holds the same token whose SHA-256 the device record already has
(`token_sha256`, `src/adapters/remote.rs:345`), looked up by
`core.device_by_token` (`src/app.rs:3127`). The certificate in
`identity.json` stays as written; the browser's certificate is made in
memory (step 2), so `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` (`src/ports/remote.rs:17`,
1 today) and `SCHEMA_VERSION` (`src/core/model.rs:12`, 16 today) do not
move. If the implementer finds a field has to be added after all, the
bump is: the value in `model.rs` or `ports/remote.rs` at implementation
time, plus one, with a step in `adapters::store::migrate`.

The page's own record lives on the device, not on the host: the pin
`{server_id, spki_sha256}` it last paired with, in `localStorage` under
try/catch (public values, so a script-readable store is fine), used only
to say "identity changed" versus "revoked". The page renders with
nothing in it.

## The signals

- `changed`/`removed`/`resync_required` are the existing frames; no new
  event, no new revision rule. The page applies §4.4 as the headset
  does: it keeps one held revision per key (`waiting`, `projects`,
  `sessions:<project>`, `session:<id>`, `conversation:<id>`,
  `screen:<id>`), applies a reply only if its envelope `revision` is at
  or past the held one, and on `epoch` change or `resync_required`
  refetches everything.
- **Live path.** Base: a timer refetches `waiting`, every expanded
  project's sessions and the open session's content, every 5 s (3 s when
  the open session is waiting). When the socket opens and `hello` lands,
  the timer relaxes to 30 s (the spec's own visible-view refetch,
  `docs/remote-client.md:256`) and `changed {waiting}`,
  `{sessions,id}`, `{session,id}` and the watched content kinds trigger
  the matching refetch at once. Metadata kinds need no `watch` frame; the
  open session sends `watch {conversation|screen, id}` and `unwatch` on
  leaving (`docs/remote-client.md:240,256`). "A session that starts
  waiting moves to the top without a reload" is `changed {waiting}` then
  a `waiting` refetch on the socket, and the next poll without it.
- **Failure words**, each one sentence in the page: a `fetch` that fails
  with no HTTP status is "The host is unreachable, or this browser does
  not trust its certificate" (facts, U2: the page never assumes the
  click-through outlives the session); a 401 on `/device` triggers
  `/info`, and a different `spki_sha256` or `server_id` from the pin is
  "Identity changed, pair again" (nothing more is sent), the same key
  with a pin stored is "This device was revoked", and no pin is the
  no-code screen; `pairing_closed`, `wrong_code` and `wrong_key` from
  `/pair` are worded plainly.

## The actions and effects

None in the core: no `AppAction`, no `Effect`, no change under
`src/core/`. The pairing window, the failure counter and `Paired`
already carry everything (`src/app.rs:3606-3665`). The work is in the
adapter and in `serve_remote`'s handlers, in this order:

1. **Spike first, `spikes/23-web-cookie/`.** CLAUDE.md requires one for a
   new risky mechanism. Do steps 2-5 minimally with a 20-line throwaway
   `web/` page that, on a `delivery: "cookie"` pair, does a `fetch` of
   `/device` and opens `new WebSocket` to `/api/v1/events`, and run it in
   Safari and Chrome on the Mac against a LAN bind (accept the warning).
   Record in the README: cookie stored, returned on `fetch`, returned on
   the upgrade, per browser and version. The owner repeats it on the
   iPhone (O1); the plan does not wait on that, the result only decides
   whether the socket ever opens there. If `fetch` fails in Safari, stop
   as in decision 2.
2. **Certificate with SANs, in memory.** Replace the single fixed cert in
   `tls_config` (`:144`, signature unchanged) with a `ResolvesServerCert`
   that holds one `CertifiedKey` and the address it was made for. On each
   handshake it compares `local_address()` (`:962`, a connected UDP
   socket, no packet sent) and re-makes the certificate over the same
   `rcgen::KeyPair::from_pem(key)` when the address moved. The
   certificate carries SANs `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1` and the
   current address, `ExtendedKeyUsage::ServerAuth`, the same CommonName,
   and a 397-day validity (facts, Settled 5: iOS 13+ limits). The key is
   the same, so `spki_sha256` is the same and `identity.json` is not
   rewritten; native clients ignore dates and names (`pinned_client`,
   `:168`). The Bonjour `.local` name is not added: the QR carries an IP.
3. **Request and reply fields** (additive, `src/adapters/remote.rs`).
   `RemoteRequest` (`:360`, one literal, in `read_request`) gains
   `cookies: Vec<(String, String)>` (only names starting `__Host-sb-`,
   so other sites' cookies never enter memory), `origin:
   Option<String>`, `host: Option<String>`. `RemoteReply` (`:389`)
   gains `set_cookie: Option<String>`; its ~11 literal sites in
   `src/app.rs` (lines 1664, 1679, 2365-2376, 2754, 3570, 3723, 3736,
   3767) and `:829` add `set_cookie: None`. `respond` (`:530`) becomes a
   thin call of a general writer taking content type, extra headers and
   a head-only flag; the status table gains nothing new.
4. **Pages on the connection thread.** In `connection` (`:770`), before
   `limited`, `remote_page::route` answers the three paths (decision 4).
   `HEAD` writes the headers with the real `Content-Length` and no body.
5. **Cookie auth, `/device`, `Origin`.** In `authenticate` (`:3127`):
   a bearer wins; otherwise the cookie named for this installation. A
   cookie-authenticated request that is not a plain `GET`, and every
   upgrade, must carry `Origin: https://<Host header>` or it is 403
   `forbidden_origin`, logged by code. An unknown cookie token is 401 as
   today, with `set_cookie` clearing the cookie (`Max-Age=0`).
   `remote_pair` (`:3606`) reads `delivery`; for `"cookie"` it omits
   `token` and sets the cookie on the reply. `serve_remote` (`:3017`)
   gains, beside `events` and after `authenticate`, `GET device` ->
   `{device_id, name, scope}` through `envelope` (any paired scope). The
   `Referrer-Policy` and the unchanged `refuse` log (path without query)
   keep the code out of the log.
6. **The invite URL.** A pure `remote::invite_url(address:
   Option<IpAddr>, port, server_id, key, code) -> String` in
   `src/adapters/remote.rs` beside `local_address`, using
   `SocketAddr::new(ip, port)` so an IPv6 address is bracketed. No
   percent-encoding: the code is Crockford, the key hex, the id a UUID
   (the undecoded query, facts, tree).
7. **Swift.** `PairingInvite.parse` (`client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/
   Info.swift:112`) tries JSON, then a URL (`URLComponents`: `code`, `key`,
   `id`, host and port into `addresses`, a host with a colon rebracketed).
   `switchboard-remote pair` and `BrowserView` call `parse` and need no
   change. Run `swift test` in `client/` on the Mac (not run in
   planning).
8. **The page** (`web/`), plain DOM, `textContent` only (session names
   and agent output are untrusted; the last response is shown as
   `white-space: pre-wrap` text, not markdown). Sessions grouped by
   project, waiting first and marked in text as well as colour; the kind,
   the card word and `waiting_reason`; the session view shows the last
   response for a Claude Code session (falling back to `screen` on
   `no conversation`) and `screen` for every other kind; a reply box that
   posts `send` `{op: <uuid>, text}` only when `/device` says `control`;
   host name and scope in the header. A reply is submitted with a fresh
   `op` and, on a timeout, a status query (`GET ops/{op}`) and never a
   resend (`docs/remote-client.md` §4.5).

## The UI

`src/ui/remote.rs`, the pairing window (`:140-220`): `payload` becomes
`remote::invite_url(...)`; the QR, "Copy invite" and the "Address" line
follow. The window's help text (`:187-195`) gains, after the existing
sentence: "A browser pairs by this QR too: it will warn about the
certificate, which is expected for a host that signs its own. The
browser cannot check the host's key the way the apps do, so pair only
from this screen. The code works once." No new widget and no
`SWITCHBOARD_SCRIPT` line: `pairing <code>` (`src/script.rs:730`)
already puts the window in this state. README's dev-aid list is
unchanged.

## The tests

- **`src/adapters/remote_page.rs` unit tests**: `route` for each path,
  `HEAD`, a `POST` (405 with `Allow`), `/index.html` and `//` (none).
- **Embedded page, `tests/remote.rs`**: `index.html` references only
  `/app.js`, `/app.css` and `data:`; no `<script>` body, no `style=`
  attribute, no `http(s)://` or `//host` URL anywhere in the three files;
  every `/api/v1/<first segment>` literal in `app.js` is in the set the
  host serves (`info`, `pair`, `device`, `projects`, `sessions`,
  `waiting`, `ops`, `events`).
- **The new paths over the real listener** (`call` at `:300` returns
  status and JSON only; add a sibling returning headers and raw body):
  200 unpaired for all three with the named `Content-Type`,
  `Cache-Control: no-store`, `nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy`, and the CSP on
  the HTML, containing no `unsafe-inline`; `HEAD` has no body and the
  right length; a query changes nothing; `/api/v1/*` allowlist test
  (`:682`) and `/info` test (`:426`) still pass untouched; the `pages`
  window answers 429 past 120.
- **The pairing flow end to end with the host's own client, as the CLI
  does** (no UI test drives a browser): take `invite_url`, parse its
  query, `GET /info` and compare `key` and `id`, `POST /pair` with
  `delivery: "cookie"` (reply has no `token`; `Set-Cookie` has `Secure`,
  `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, `Path=/`, the `__Host-sb-` name), then
  with only the cookie: `GET /device` (scope), `GET /waiting`, `POST
  .../send` with the right `Origin` (control) and with a wrong one (403),
  `GET` of `events` upgrade with the right `Origin` (101, `hello`) and a
  wrong one (403); a bearer request is unchanged and a bearer wins over a
  wrong cookie; a read-scope device's `send` is 403 `scope`; revoke ->
  the next cookie request is 401 and the reply clears the cookie, and the
  subscriber is closed; key rotation -> 401 and `/info` shows the new key.
- **Certificate**: a rustls client with the stock webpki verifier and the
  presented certificate as its only anchor connects by `localhost`,
  `127.0.0.1` and the current `local_address()` (skips cleanly when there
  is no address), and `spki_sha256` is the same before and after a
  re-issue. If the webpki client will not take an end-entity anchor,
  fall back to parsing the SANs from the DER.
- **`invite_url`** unit test: IPv4, IPv6 (bracketed), no address.
- **`tests/ui.rs:7424`** (`remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device`):
  the copied invite is now the URL; assert it starts `https://`, has the
  window's code, key and id, and no JSON.
- **Fixtures**: add `client/Fixtures/invite_url.txt`, written by
  `write_fixtures` (`tests/remote.rs:1587`) from `invite_url`, decoded by
  a new `FixturesTests.swift` case through `PairingInvite.parse`
  (extends `the_client_fixtures_decode_on_both_sides`, `:1829`). `/device`
  gets no fixture: no Swift speaker reads it.
- **Not testable here, said plainly**: the page's script runs in no test
  (no browser, no JS runner, and the plan adds neither). Its logic is
  checked by the acceptance steps below, run by hand in a real browser
  on a LAN bind, and kept to small pure functions.
- **Acceptance by hand**: `cargo run --locked`; Remote devices, LAN,
  allow pairing with `control`; scan on a phone, accept the warning,
  see sessions; a session that starts waiting moves up (on the poll if
  the socket does not open); send a reply and watch it arrive in the
  pane; revoke the phone and see "revoked" on its next refresh. Also
  open the same QR text in Safari and Chrome on the Mac.

## Docs, in the same commit

- `docs/remote-client.md`: §4.1 bounds (three page paths, the `pages`
  window, answered on the connection thread); §4.3 table (the three
  `GET` page paths and `GET /api/v1/device`); §5 (the pre-pairing line;
  the token sentence: bearer over the pinned connection **or** the
  host-set HttpOnly cookie for a browser, still never in a URL; the QR
  is the URL; the browser-trust paragraph from decision 1; the Origin
  rule); `:207` (the excerpt is not a `SessionView` field); §9 untouched.
- `docs/design.md`: a "Web control surface" item in the Remote client
  status section (from `:3107`), with the known gaps: no excerpt on the
  wire, Safari socket unreliable, browser pairing not pinned, U1 as
  measured in the spike.
- `README.md`: Layout table lines for `src/adapters/remote.rs` (`:383`),

  new `web/` entry, and `spikes/23-web-cookie`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, under Unreleased: "A browser can pair and control the
  host from the pairing window's QR code."

## For the owner, after this lands

- O1: on the iPhone or iPad, state the iOS version, does the cookie

  the script is the follow-up; if the socket works, the poll relaxes to

## Commit message

`Serve a browser control page from the remote port, paired by a URL QR and an HttpOnly cookie`

## Contract additions

- `RemoteRequest`: `cookies: Vec<(String, String)>`, `origin:

- `RemoteReply`: `set_cookie: Option<String>`.
- `POST /api/v1/pair`: optional body field `delivery` (`"cookie"`); with
